Construct an environmental data schema

Source: R/schema.R
env_schema.Rd

Creates an `env_schema` object by attaching environmental column mappings and schema metadata to a data frame.

Usage

env_schema(
  df,
  site = NULL,
  location,
  date,
  analyte,
  result,
  unit = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  reporting_flag = NULL,
  reporting_limit = NULL,
  detection_limit = NULL,
  quantitation_limit = NULL,
  achieved_mdc = NULL,
  measurement_uncertainty = NULL,
  method = NULL,
  analysis_date = NULL,
  matrix = NULL,
  lab_name = NULL,
  metadata = NULL,
  qualifier_table = NULL,
  display_options = default_display_options(),
  analyte_lookup = analyte_tbl
)

Arguments

df

Data frame.

site

Site identifier column.

location

Location identifier column.

date

Sample date column.

analyte

Analyte column.

result

Analytical result column.

unit

Unit column.

sample_id

Sample identifier column.

reporting_flag

Laboratory qualifier column.

reporting_limit

Reporting limit column.

detection_limit

Detection limit column.

quantitation_limit

Quantitation limit column (PQL, LOQ, SQL, etc.).

achieved_mdc

Achieved minimum detectable concentration (radiochemistry).

measurement_uncertainty

Measurement uncertainty column.

method

Analytical method column.

analysis_date

Analysis date column.

matrix

Matrix column.

lab_name

Laboratory column.

metadata

Optional tidyselect specification identifying columns containing method-specific metadata.

qualifier_table

Optional qualifier lookup table.

analyte_lookup

Optional analyte metadata lookup table. Defaults to analyte_tbl. Used to standardize analyte names, assign analyte identifiers, and attach analyte metadata.

Value

A tibble with class `env_schema`.

The returned object retains all original source columns and stores environmental column mappings in object metadata.

Additional manager-generated columns may include:

.analysis_result

Standardized analytical value used for calculations.

.censored

Logical censoring indicator.

.display_threshold

Threshold used when constructing display-ready censored values. Reporting limits are preferred, followed by quantitation limits, detection limits, and finally the analytical result itself.

.display_threshold_type

Source of the display threshold. One of `"reporting_limit"`, `"quantitation_limit"`, `"detection_limit"`, or `"analysis_result"`.

.display_result

Display-ready reporting result suitable for tables and exports.

Details

Source column names are preserved and their environmental meaning is stored in schema metadata, allowing downstream plotting, reporting, trend analysis, geochemical calculations, censored-data methods, and radiochemistry workflows to operate on a consistent environmental data model.

`env_schema()` does not rename or modify source data columns.

Instead, the environmental meaning of each source column is stored as schema metadata through an internal column-mapping structure.

For example:


env_schema(
  data,
  location = location_id,
  date = sample_date,
  analyte = parameter,
  result = concentration
)

records that `location_id` contains location identifiers, `sample_date` contains sample dates, `parameter` contains analyte names, and `concentration` contains analytical results.

The constructor may also create standardized derived columns used internally by manager for result classification, analyte metadata, reporting workflows, plotting, and statistical calculations.

Stored schema mappings can be inspected using `schema_mapping()`.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
gw <- env_schema(
  my_data,
  location = location_id,
  date = sample_date,
  analyte = param_name,
  result = analysis_result,
  unit = default_unit
)

schema_mapping(gw)
} # }
